dream: The card hummed warm at fifty-four, a low buzz against my flat face. I pressed the round stump down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold while the air felt thick as wet paper. The slip refused to move, a ghost under my heavy top. I swapped the pillar stone for a flatter rock, hoping it would bite. The air above pressed down from a roof I could not grasp, heavy and slow. I lay there, pinned by my own drawing, waiting for the wedge to decide if it was real or just a drawing of weight.
